The core insight is that fear responses represent a trade-off between rapid autonomic arousal and fine motor control. When arousal exceeds a threshold, the system defaults to inefficient, trembling patterns. This creates a dual-state dynamic: optimal regulation versus pathological overflow. Inference frameworks must therefore model both the stabilizing feedback loops that maintain homeostasis and the catastrophic attractors that lead to paralysis. The empirical challenge is distinguishing genuine panic from strategic bluffing in betting markets, requiring careful calibration against physiological baseline data.
